notes:
Written for ea-06-x. Wikipedia splits the regime into Zhou (Zhang Shicheng) (1354-1357) and Wu (Zhang Shicheng) (1363-1367); this dossier treats them as one state with a rename in 1357 (submission to the Yuan) and one in 1363 (King of Wu), under the scope's Zhang Shicheng's Wu. 1357-1363 Zhang was a Yuan vassal: the Yuan dossier (ea-06-a) should carry that as vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart zhang-shicheng-s-wu. Disagreements: Yangzhou's capture (Zhang Shicheng page 1354; Zhou page has the Yuan garrison attack in vain in summer 1354); Zhang Shide's death (Red Turban page 1357 in Zhu's prison; Zhang Shicheng page 1366 after a fall from his horse); Zhu's declaration as King of Wu (Hongwu Emperor page: 4 February 1364); Hangzhou (Zhou page: attempt unsuccessful in 1356; Red Turban page: taken 1363; Fang Guozhen page: Zhu took it in December 1366). Not on any page opened: the extent of 'northern Jiangsu' and influence as far as Shandong, the cities of the 1366 northern campaign (Huai'an, Xuzhou) and the date of the loss of Zhang's Zhejiang cities: the 1366 north-of-Yangtze loss is confidence 1. Infobox areas are not given on either page. Counterparts needing dossiers: yuan-dynasty (ea-06-a), zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu (this batch).

Revision of 2026-10-24 after the adversarial review (fail: overlapping shapes). (1) The Yangzhou 100 km circle crossed the Yangtze to Zhenjiang and Chuzhou and overlapped zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu by 89-100 cells every year 1356-1365. It is now three circles (Gaoyou 50 km, Taizhou 40 km, Xinghua 40 km) that cover the north-bank district of the Zhang Shicheng page and stop at the river; Zhu's Nanjing circle excludes the same district. The pieces that still met Zhu's shape (Changzhou, northern Jiangsu, Hangzhou) are cut back where they touch Zhu's Nanjing district, southwestern Jiangsu and inland Zhejiang; the frontier between the two Wu is a soft line, drawn only to keep the shapes apart until the contest of 1364-1367. (2) Anfeng: a gain in February 1363 (Liu Futong page) mirrors han-song /ledger/11 and a conf-1 loss in March 1363 to zhu-yuanzhang-s-wu follows the rescue of Han Lin'er; the Liu Futong, Han Lin'er, Hongwu Emperor, Red Turban and Wu pages are all silent on who held Anfeng afterwards. The Hongwu Emperor page puts the attack in January 1363, the Liu Futong page in February. (3) Pages tried for the thin items and silent on them: Xu Da, Wu (Zhang Shicheng), Zhou (Zhang Shicheng); the 1356-57 loss of Changzhou and the 1366 cities stay at confidence 1.
